n=λ+1>0 and card(I)=n. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V; e_0=v. For every integer m≥0, h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v; for m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v. The vectors y^m v vanish for m>λ. The action matrices are xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all r≥0 and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise. All these divided-power matrix coefficients are integers.

ι_R:M_R→V is injective, its image spans V over ℂ, and M_R is free of rank n over R. Under this embedding M_R is stable under all X_r,Y_r (r≥0). For every integer t with 0≤t≤λ, t! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M and give its induced Chevalley action after tensoring.
There exists b∈J with b≠0 such that J=Rb. For any such b, the vectors (b e_i)_{i∈I} form an R-basis of M_R (identified with its image under ι_R), of cardinality n>0.

argument.text: For every integer d not divisible by p its image in K is nonzero, because H002 says the kernel of ℤ→K is pℤ. Thus define ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). Equality of fractions is preserved by cross-multiplication, so this is well-defined and preserves sums and products; it extends ℤ→K. The characteristic also factors the integer map through ℱ_p=ℤ/pℤ; primality H001 makes this a field, and its map into K is injective since a unital map from a field has zero kernel. On elementary tensors define A:M⊗_ℤK→M_R⊗_R K by A(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. The balancing relations in the two tensor products verify well-definedness; the inverse identities follow on the displayed generators, since (r⊗m)⊗c=(1⊗m)⊗ρ(r)c. These generators span, so A is a K-linear isomorphism.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K, ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d), is a ring map extending ℤ→K, and the map A:V(K)→M_R⊗_R K given by m⊗c↦(1⊗m)⊗c is a K-linear isomorphism with inverse (r⊗m)⊗c↦m⊗ρ(r)c.

argument.text: The kernel of ρ is pR: for a/d∈R, its image is zero exactly when p divides a, equivalently a/d belongs to pR. Its image is the prime field ℱ_p, because a/d reduces to the quotient of two prime-field elements. Thus R/pR≃ℱ_p. The map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K sends u⊗c to [u]⊗c. Conversely define [u]⊗c↦u⊗c. A different lift u+pw gives the same tensor since (pw)⊗c=w⊗pc=0. Balancing over ℱ_p is valid: lift a prime-field scalar to r∈R and use (ru)⊗c=u⊗ρ(r)c; changing its lift by pR has no effect. These formulas define inverse K-linear maps on the simple tensors. This proves the second isomorphism as well as its compatibility with the first one.

produces.statement: R/pR≃ℱ_p via ρ, and B:M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K is the K-linear isomorphism u⊗c↦[u]⊗c with inverse [u]⊗c↦u⊗c.

argument.text: Choose b as in N004 and define β_i=A^{-1}((b e_i)⊗1). M001 with A=R, B=K and basis (b e_i) gives the K-basis 1⊗b e_i of K⊗_R M_R; the tensor flip sends it to (b e_i)⊗1 in M_R⊗_R K. The flip is an isomorphism because u⊗c↦c⊗u and its reverse are balanced and their composites fix all simple tensors. Transporting along A^{-1} therefore shows that β is a K-basis of V(K). M002 over K counts it: dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0 by N001. Also the quotient M_R/pM_R has the basis [b e_i] over R/pR: coordinates in the R-basis of N004 reduce independently, since a combination lies in pM_R exactly when every coefficient lies in pR. Thus β is precisely the reduced basis extended from ℱ_p to K as in the supplied proof.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of V(K) indexed by I, dim_K V(K)=n>0; it is the scalar extension to K of the ℱ_p-basis [b e_i] of M_R/pM_R.

argument.text: N001 gives all action formulas on e_i; complex linearity gives the identical formulas on b e_i. N002 says the operators preserve M_R and x,y,h preserve M. The maps A and B above commute with every induced lattice operator: check this on m⊗c and u⊗c using their defining formulas. Therefore the x,y,h formulas on β and the X_r,Y_r formulas are exactly those of N001 with each integer coefficient replaced by its image in K. Explicitly xβ_0=0, xβ_i=bar(λ-i+1)β_{i-1}, yβ_i=bar(i+1)β_{i+1} until yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=bar(λ-2i)β_i; X_r and Y_r have respectively coefficients bar(binom(λ-i+r,r)) and bar(binom(i+r,r)) in their stated ranges and zero outside. For 0≤r≤λ, N002 makes r! a unit in R, so its image is nonzero in the field K. The integer-operator identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold on M and persist after tensoring. Thus X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r.

produces.statement: On β one has xβ_0=0, xβ_i=bar(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ; yβ_i=bar(i+1)β_{i+1} for 0≤i<λ; yβ_λ=0; hβ_i=bar(λ-2i)β_i for i∈I. For all r≥0, X_rβ_i=bar(binom(λ-i+r,r))β_{i-r} for r≤i and is zero for r>i; Y_rβ_i=bar(binom(i+r,r))β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise. For 0≤r≤λ the scalar bar(r!) is nonzero and X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r, Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r on V(K).

argument.text: N002 expresses E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j} with the scalar a unit in R. Since E_ij(b e_k) is b e_i for k=j and zero otherwise, tensoring this identity yields the coordinate matrix unit T_ij on β with formula T_ij=bar(binom(λ,j))^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Its scalar is nonzero after reduction, since a unit maps to a unit. For an arbitrary K-subspace W temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under x,y. It is then invariant under their nonnegative powers, their scalar multiples, and their compositions. Every divided power appearing in this formula has index between 0 and λ, so F004 shows that it preserves W. Consequently every T_ij preserves W. Discharge L1 and quantify over W. This proves the tensor identifications, reduced basis and formulas, and the matrix-unit invariance assertion.
